title: Novena to St. Francis of Assisi
description: A nine-day prayer for peace, simplicity, and a deeper love for God's creation. St. Francis is the patron saint of animals, ecology, and peacemakers, known for his radical poverty, love of nature, and devotion to Christ crucified.
intention: For peace, environmental concerns, simplicity of life, and a deeper love for all creation
instructions: Pray this novena for 9 consecutive days with an open heart. St. Francis is especially invoked for peace in troubled situations, for those struggling with materialism, for environmental concerns, and for a deeper appreciation of God's creation. Include your personal intentions, particularly for peace, simplicity, and care for creation.
background_info: St. Francis was born Giovanni di Pietro di Bernardone in 1181 or 1182 in Assisi, Italy. The son of a wealthy cloth merchant, he lived a carefree youth until a conversion experience led him to renounce his inheritance and embrace radical poverty. He founded the Franciscan Order, founded the Order of Poor Clares with St. Clare, and preached the Gospel with simplicity and joy. He received the stigmata (the wounds of Christ) in 1224, becoming the first recorded person to receive this gift. He wrote the Canticle of the Sun, praising God through Brother Sun, Sister Moon, and all creation. He is known for preaching to birds, taming a wolf, and his love for all creatures. He died in 1226 and was canonized just two years later.

days.title: Day 1: Detachment from Worldly Things
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Francis, you who gave up your family's wealth to embrace radical poverty, teach me to hold lightly to the things of this world. You understood that attachment to possessions can possess us, while simplicity sets us free. Help me to examine my own attachments and to simplify my life. May I find my treasure not in things but in God alone. Pray for me, that I may have the courage to let go of whatever keeps me from fully following Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Francis, pray for us and teach us the way of simplicity.
days.reflection: Francis literally stripped off his fine clothes in the town square of Assisi, declaring that he now had only one Father in heaven. This dramatic act symbolized his complete detachment from material possessions. He called poverty his 'lady' and found in simplicity a freedom that wealth can never provide. What attachments might God be calling you to surrender?
days.intention_prayer: St. Francis, help me to identify and release my attachments: [name what you are holding too tightly]. Teach me the freedom of simplicity.
days.scripture: "Then he said to them all: 'Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.'" - Luke 9:23

days.title: Day 2: Brother Sun and Sister Moon
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Francis, poet of creation, you saw all of nature as a mirror of God's glory. You called the sun Brother and the moon Sister, recognizing that all creatures praise God simply by being what He made them to be. Help me to see creation with your eyes of wonder. May I join my voice with all creatures in praising the Creator. Give me a heart that delights in the beauty of the natural world and a will to care for it. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Francis, pray for us and teach us the way of simplicity.
days.reflection: Francis's Canticle of the Sun is one of the oldest poems in Italian literature. It praises God through Brother Sun, Sister Moon, Brother Wind, Sister Water, Brother Fire, and even Sister Death. Francis saw all creation as a family joined in praising God. When we appreciate creation with this attitude, everything becomes a reminder of the Creator.
days.intention_prayer: St. Francis, open my eyes to the wonder of creation. Help me to praise God through the beauty around me: [express your appreciation for creation].
days.scripture: "The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands." - Psalm 19:1

days.title: Day 3: The Wolf of Gubbio
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Francis, peacemaker, you tamed the wolf that terrorized the town of Gubbio. You saw past the beast's ferocity to find a creature needing food and understanding. You brokered peace between the wolf and the townspeople, calling the animal 'Brother Wolf.' Help me to be a peacemaker in my own conflicts. Give me the courage to approach what frightens me, the wisdom to seek understanding, and the grace to reconcile enemies. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Francis, pray for us and teach us the way of simplicity.
days.reflection: The story of the Wolf of Gubbio shows Francis's approach to conflict and fear. Rather than destroying the 'enemy,' he sought understanding and peace. The wolf was hungry and had been mistreated. Both sides needed to change. Francis brought them together in an agreement that benefited all. True peacemaking requires courage, understanding, and willingness to compromise.
days.intention_prayer: St. Francis, I pray for peace in my conflicts: [name specific conflicts]. Help me to be an instrument of peace and reconciliation.
days.scripture: "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God." - Matthew 5:9

days.title: Day 4: Preaching the Gospel
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Francis, you sent your brothers out two by two to preach the Gospel, instructing them to 'preach the Gospel always, and if necessary, use words.' Your life was itself a sermon of love, simplicity, and joy. Help me to be a witness to Christ through my actions more than my words. May my life preach the Gospel to all I meet. Give me words when needed, but more importantly, give me the love that speaks louder than any sermon. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Francis, pray for us and teach us the way of simplicity.
days.reflection: The famous saying attributed to Francis – 'Preach the Gospel always; if necessary, use words' – captures his approach to evangelization. He did preach, but it was his life that drew people to Christ. His poverty, joy, simplicity, and love were irresistible. We, too, preach by how we live – our choices, our treatment of others, our priorities.
days.intention_prayer: St. Francis, help me to preach the Gospel by my life. Show me how to witness to Christ through my actions: [commit to a specific way of witnessing].
days.scripture: "In the same way, let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven." - Matthew 5:16

days.title: Day 5: The Cross of San Damiano
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Francis, you heard Christ speak to you from the cross of San Damiano: 'Go, Francis, rebuild my house.' You obeyed literally, rebuilding chapels, but later understood that Christ meant you to rebuild His Church spiritually. Help me to hear Christ's call to serve Him in His Church. Show me where He wants me to rebuild, repair, or renew. Give me the courage to respond generously to His invitation. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Francis, pray for us and teach us the way of simplicity.
days.reflection: The crucifix of San Damiano changed Francis's life. He heard Christ calling him to 'rebuild my house, which is falling into ruin.' At first, Francis thought this meant buildings. Only gradually did he understand the spiritual mission. God often calls us to something specific, and the full meaning unfolds over time. Listening and responding are the first steps.
days.intention_prayer: St. Francis, help me to hear and respond to Christ's call. Show me how I can help rebuild His Church: [express your desire to serve].
days.scripture: "He said to them, 'Go into all the world and preach the gospel to all creation.'" - Mark 16:15

days.title: Day 6: The Stigmata
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Francis, you who received the stigmata, the wounds of Christ, in your own body, teach me the mystery of sharing in Christ's suffering. You so identified with Christ crucified that your body bore His wounds. Help me to understand that following Jesus means sharing both His cross and His resurrection. May I not shrink from suffering but unite mine to His for the salvation of souls. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Francis, pray for us and teach us the way of simplicity.
days.reflection: In 1224, while praying on Mount La Verna during a forty-day fast, Francis received the stigmata – the five wounds of Christ in his hands, feet, and side. He was the first known person to receive this gift. It was the culmination of a life of radical identification with Christ. His body literally bore the marks of Jesus. We, too, are called to bear Christ to the world, even if not so visibly.
days.intention_prayer: St. Francis, unite my sufferings to Christ's. Help me to carry my cross with love: [offer your sufferings to God].
days.scripture: "I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me." - Galatians 2:20

days.title: Day 7: The Manger at Greccio
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Francis, you created the first Christmas manger scene at Greccio to make the Incarnation tangible for simple people. You wanted them to see, smell, and touch the reality of God becoming man. Help me to enter more deeply into the mystery of the Incarnation. May the reality of God-with-us transform my faith from abstract to concrete, from distant to intimate. Let me marvel that God became man for love of me. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Francis, pray for us and teach us the way of simplicity.
days.reflection: Francis's Christmas celebration at Greccio in 1223 began the tradition of nativity scenes. He wanted people to experience the Incarnation viscerally – not just as a doctrinal truth but as a lived reality. A real manger, real animals, a real infant. The Incarnation means God entered into our physical world. Francis's spirituality was earthy and incarnational, not abstract and spiritualized.
days.intention_prayer: St. Francis, deepen my faith in the Incarnation. Let me marvel at God becoming man: [express your wonder at the mystery of Christmas].
days.scripture: "The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14

days.title: Day 8: Care for Creation
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Francis, patron of ecology, you saw all creatures as brothers and sisters under one Creator. You preached to birds, befriended animals, and honored the natural world as a gift from God. In our time, creation suffers from neglect and exploitation. Help me to be a better steward of the earth. Show me how to care for creation in practical ways, to reduce my environmental impact, and to advocate for the protection of nature. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Francis, pray for us and teach us the way of simplicity.
days.reflection: Francis is the patron saint of ecologists because of his love for all creation. He saw himself as part of nature, not above it. He called creatures 'brother' and 'sister.' This was not sentimentality but profound theology: all things come from one Creator and all should be treated with respect. Environmental care is a Christian duty, not just a political issue.
days.intention_prayer: St. Francis, guide me in caring for creation. Show me practical ways to honor the earth as a gift from God: [commit to specific environmental actions].
days.scripture: "Then God said, 'Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the wild animals, and over all the creatures that move along the ground.'" - Genesis 1:26

days.title: Day 9: Perfect Joy
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Francis, you taught that perfect joy is not found in great accomplishments or spiritual privileges but in bearing trials with patience and love. You said that if you returned to your friary in the freezing rain, were turned away at the door, and still responded with love, you would have perfect joy. Help me to find joy not in favorable circumstances but in union with Christ. May I have the joy that comes from loving unconditionally, even when unloved in return. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Francis, pray for us and teach us the way of simplicity.
days.reflection: Francis's teaching on 'perfect joy' was counterintuitive. He rejected the obvious sources of happiness – miracles, learning, great deeds – and identified true joy as patient endurance of suffering with love. Joy is not the absence of pain but the presence of Christ within it. This is the joy that no circumstance can take away.
days.intention_prayer: St. Francis, teach me the secret of perfect joy. Help me to find joy in loving and serving, regardless of my circumstances: [express your desire for this deep joy].
days.scripture: "Consider it pure joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of many kinds, because you know that the testing of your faith produces perseverance." - James 1:2-3

source: Traditional Catholic Devotion to St. Francis of Assisi
notes: St. Francis is one of the most beloved saints in Christian history. He is the patron saint of animals, ecology, the environment, Italy, merchants, and stowaways. His feast day, October 4, is often celebrated with blessing of animals ceremonies. The prayer attributed to him, 'Lord, make me an instrument of your peace,' captures his spirit, though it was likely written in his honor rather than by him. His radical way of following Christ continues to inspire millions.
